text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it aims to build up a seamless global cargo network with selected airline and forwarder partners.

Michael Kraus, cargo business development and global accounts manager, said at a news conference: "In 2000 there will be two or three airline systems both in passenger and cargo which will compete with each other."
To meet this challenge, Lufthansa planned to establish a rapid, reliable and high-performance door-to-door transport network, he explained.

"Lufthansa alone cannot achieve this but in partnership with three, four or five airlines we can do it. This could mean that we do not fly everything but we fly for others and others fly for us," he said.
Kraus noted cargo airline partners did not need to be the same ones as in passenger alliances since it was not always easy to find synergies.
Lufthansa Cargo already operates joint freighter services with strategic partners Thai Airways International, Varig and South African Airways SAA.CN and co-operates closely with DHL International.
But cargo co-operation with alliance partners United Airlines and SAS has proved more difficult to get off the ground, industry sources said.
Kraus said long-established cargo partnerships such as with Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Japan Airlines Co Ltd were essentially joint ventures to control market capacity on specific routes.
He gave no details of forthcoming new or altered partnerships. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
